title: Bot is executing momentum/trend trades disguised as mean reversion signals
analysis: Two submitted trades violate the strategy's core identity. On 2026-05-15, NVDA was bought with signals ['RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)'] — every single signal is a momentum/trend indicator, the exact opposite of mean reversion. Signal score was 4, confidence MEDIUM, and the trade was SUBMITTED. On 2026-05-18, AAPL was bought with signals ['RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)', 'A_GRADE setup'] — again, zero mean reversion signals, yet executed. Critically, the NVDA entry fired on ADX>25, which Rule 6 explicitly forbids ('If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals'). The signal scoring system awards points for RSI<35, RSI<45, BelowBB, BelowMA20 — yet the bot is somehow scoring +4 on RSI>65 and AboveMA20, suggesting either the scoring engine has drifted or a parallel undocumented scoring path exists. These are not edge cases — both trades were SUBMITTED with capital at risk. Meanwhile, the same sessions show legitimate mean reversion signals on META and MSFT being correctly rejected for position duplication. The bot is selectively enforcing rules.
rationale: A strategy that executes both mean reversion AND momentum entries without an explicit regime-switching framework is not two strategies — it is an uncontrolled strategy. The NVDA and AAPL entries lack the disciplined entry criteria that make mean reversion statistically profitable. If momentum trades are intended, they require separate rules: trend confirmation, different stop placement (ATR trailing vs fixed level), different position sizing, and different exit logic. Running them through the mean reversion framework produces miscalibrated stops and targets. The 0.5x ATR hard stop designed for a mean reversion snap-back is dangerously tight for a momentum position that needs room to develop. This is the single highest-risk structural flaw in the current system.

insight.why_now: Both contaminating trades occurred in the most recent 7 days of the journal (May 15 and May 18). This is not historical noise — it is the current operational state of the bot. The NVDA trade on May 15 was entered while the account was up $243 on the day, suggesting the bot is reaching for trades when the session is going well.
insight.purpose: Enforce strict signal identity: every submitted trade must only fire mean reversion signals. Momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveMA20, ADX>25) must either be explicitly blocked from producing BUY actions, or routed to a clearly separate, separately governed strategy module.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminates the most dangerous category of rule violation — trades that appear valid by score but are structurally misaligned. Prevents the mean reversion risk framework (tight ATR stops, MA20 targets) from being misapplied to momentum positions where it systematically underestimates required stop distance.
insight.risks: If the momentum trades have been profitable (cannot be confirmed from this journal slice since no close data is shown), adding this guardrail may temporarily reduce trade frequency. However, the structural risk of an un-governed momentum trade experiencing a gap-down while sized and stopped as a mean reversion trade outweighs any short-term frequency loss.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 25, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. HARD BLOCK: Any signal set containing RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, or ADX>25 (trending) must result in SKIP regardless of signal score. These are momentum signals and are structurally incompatible with mean reversion entry logic, stop placement, and exit targets. Log as 'MOMENTUM_SIGNAL_BLOCKED' for review.

title: Universe concentration in 3 correlated mega-cap tech names is causing opportunity starvation
analysis: Of 50 journal entries, the only symbols generating signals above threshold are META, MSFT, NVDA, and AAPL — all large-cap technology stocks with correlation typically above 0.75 during risk-off episodes. The system held META and MSFT simultaneously for multiple days (open_positions persistently = 2 across May 12-14), meaning effective portfolio heat is concentrated in a single factor: large-cap tech sentiment. This correlation means the 5-position limit and 1.5% per-trade risk rule provide less diversification protection than they appear to — two positions at 1.5% risk each, if 0.80 correlated, behave like a single 2.7% risk position by variance. The watchlist starvation is also visible in the rejection pattern: on May 13 alone, the bot generated 5 BUY signals across only META and MSFT, all rejected because both were already held. The bot had valid signal energy but zero eligible instruments to deploy it into. Sector data shows Energy +4.96% over 5 days — the strongest performer — yet no energy names appear anywhere in the journal. Healthcare -0.13% and Financials +0.32% suggest sector mean reversion opportunities exist outside tech that the watchlist cannot access.
rationale: Mean reversion works best on instruments with documented range-bound behavior and high liquidity. Diversified ETFs (SPY, QQQ, XLE, GLD, TLT) have superior mean reversion properties because their underlying diversification suppresses trend persistence. Adding sector ETFs would (1) reduce inter-position correlation from ~0.80 to ~0.30-0.40, (2) provide eligible instruments when individual tech names are already held, (3) naturally capture the sector rotation visible in the macro data (Energy strength, Tech weakness), and (4) give the bot valid deployment channels for the signal energy currently wasted on duplicate-position rejections. XLE in particular is directly relevant given the 5-day +4.96% Energy outperformance — a mean reversion opportunity in a sector showing relative strength divergence from the rest of the market.

insight.why_now: The May 13 session produced 5 rejected BUY signals in a single day — all blocked by the no-duplicate-position rule. This is not a parameter problem; it is a universe problem. The system is generating alpha signals it cannot act on. Simultaneously, sector data shows the strongest 5-day performer (Energy, +4.96%) is entirely absent from the tradeable universe.
insight.purpose: Expand the watchlist to include 4-6 liquid sector ETFs and broad-market ETFs with proven mean reversion characteristics, reducing intra-portfolio correlation and providing eligible instruments when individual names are blocked.
insight.expected_effect: Reduction in wasted signal cycles (currently estimated at 5+ per day based on May 13 data). Correlation-adjusted portfolio risk drops from effective ~2.7% (two correlated tech positions) toward the intended ~3% across genuinely diversified positions. Capture of sector rotation mean reversion opportunities currently invisible to the system.
insight.risks: ETFs have tighter intraday ranges than individual stocks, which may reduce R:R ratios achievable on individual trades. The 1.5:1 R:R gate (Rule 9) must be validated against historical ATR data for proposed ETF additions before live deployment. GLD and TLT in particular have lower volatility profiles that may produce frequent R:R rejections under the current 1.5:1 minimum.

proposed_rule: WATCHLIST RULE (NEW): The tradeable universe must include at minimum: (a) 3-5 individual large-cap equities across at least 2 sectors, AND (b) 3-4 sector/broad ETFs from the following approved list: SPY, QQQ, XLE, XLF, XLV, GLD, TLT. No single sector may represent more than 2 simultaneously open positions. Before adding any new symbol, confirm 90-day ADX median < 25 and 90-day historical mean reversion frequency (price returning to MA20 within 5 days after >1.5% deviation) > 55%.

title: VIX at 18.48 with tech sector weakness requires a tightened entry threshold, not standard operation
analysis: Current VIX is 18.48, classified as 'elevated' in the macro context. This sits in the transitional band between complacency (<15) and fear (>25) — historically the most unstable zone for mean reversion strategies. SPY is above its 20-day MA (737.81 vs 725.26, +1.73%), which is constructive, but sector rotation data tells a different story: Technology -0.72%, Industrials -2.13% over 5 days, while Energy +4.96%. This divergence pattern — defensive/commodity sectors outperforming growth/cyclical — is a classic early risk-off rotation signature. The bot's current watchlist is 100% tech (META, MSFT, NVDA, AAPL), meaning it is running mean reversion entries into the weakest-performing sector during a risk-off rotation. The MSFT SELL on May 18 (day_pl_at_decision: -$306.95 at time of sell) and the persistent negative P&L on May 18 (reaching -$354.92 intraday) suggest the existing tech positions are being held into sector-level headwinds. The current ADX trend filter threshold of ADX>30 is too permissive for the current macro environment — at VIX 18.48 with sector rotation active, ADX>25 signals should already be blocking entries, but Rule 6 only blocks at ADX>30.
rationale: Mean reversion in a sector experiencing active institutional outflows is not mean reversion — it is catching a falling knife. The MA20 target assumes price will revert to a stable mean, but during sector rotation the 20-day MA itself is declining, making the 'mean' a moving target in the wrong direction. A VIX-adjusted signal threshold — requiring a higher minimum score during elevated VIX regimes — adds a second layer of protection beyond the ADX filter. This is not a parameter change to scoring thresholds (handled by the specialist) but a structural regime-gating rule that activates/deactivates based on macro conditions.

insight.why_now: The combination of VIX=18.48 (elevated), Technology sector -0.72% over 5 days (the bot's entire watchlist), and Industrials -2.13% suggests the market is in early-stage risk rotation. The May 18 session ended with day P&L at -$354.92 before partial recovery — the largest intraday drawdown visible in the journal. This is occurring as the bot attempts mean reversion entries in a sector under distribution pressure.
insight.purpose: Implement a macro regime gate that raises the effective entry bar when VIX is in the 17-25 range AND the primary watchlist sectors show negative 5-day performance. This is distinct from parameter tuning — it is a binary gate that pauses new entries or requires higher conviction during unfavorable macro conditions.
insight.expected_effect: Reduction in entries during sector downtrends where mean reversion assumptions break down. The May 13 rejected MSFT entries (which the bot correctly blocked due to existing position, but would otherwise have entered) were attempted while MSFT was already under pressure — a macro gate would have added a second layer of rejection. Expected reduction in maximum adverse excursion on open positions during risk-off episodes.
insight.risks: Over-filtering during elevated VIX can cause the system to miss the highest-quality mean reversion setups, which often occur precisely when fear is elevated and stocks are maximally oversold. The gate must be calibrated to block marginal setups (score=2-3) while still permitting high-conviction entries (score=4+) even during VIX 17-25 conditions.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER AND MACRO GATE: (a) If ADX > 25, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. (b) MACRO OVERLAY: If VIX > 17 AND the primary sector of the candidate symbol shows negative 5-day performance, require signal_score ≥ 4 (elevated threshold) before entry. If VIX > 25, suspend all new entries regardless of signal score and log as 'HIGH_FEAR_REGIME_PAUSE'. Log all macro-gated skips as 'MACRO_GATE_SKIP' with VIX and sector_5d values recorded for weekly review.
